projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Marcella Balbach was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Today, I'm going to interview Marcella Balbach. She is a citizen who worked in the office of the Evansville shipyards where they built the LST ships. These ships were used for landing on coastlines of the battlefields in World War II. We are in Dale, Indiana, and today is April 26th, 2003. Marcella was born in the country of--in Dale, Indiana, on October 5th, 1921. Interviewer (?Craig Gross?), grandson of veteran Louis(ph) Balbach and Marcella Balbach. During your time of service, what did you do to help the war efforts?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: I worked. Was that on there already, that I worked in the office at--okay. Well, what else we did, we had rations. Is that anything to do with--we had rations for shoes. We could only have so many pair of shoes in a certain amount of time. We could only have so much, the groceries, so much sugar we were allowed to buy, and we were only allowed to have so much gas for the cars, and if we didn't have enough, we just couldn't drive them. That's it.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Now, during your service, what was going on during the war? Like, what were the major events that happened that you can remember?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Major events. I don't know. The only, when the war started, was Pearl Harbor. Can that be anything to do--that was the start, and I was in high school. I was a freshman when we were called to the assembly--we called it assembly, I don't know why--and we were told that war had begun, and one of our boys from the Dale area was in the Arizona, and he was killed. Now that, I don't know, that ___.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: What was the first day of your work like?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Well, kind of like any other. We had to keep tab, check on, on the ones that were on, on the working list, if they were there to do their work, and that's about all. Check--you know, it wasn't really that great. It was in the wintertime, I remember, but I don't know what--but there wasn't that much to it, really, I'll tell you the truth. It was mostly--I'm not talking on there, am I? It was not a hard job, what I done. But they did have hard jobs, the ones that worked on the ships. You know what I mean? They had....

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: What things do you remember from your first days, like the main events that you did?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: First what, now?

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Like, what were the major events that happened that you can remember around your work area?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: ___+ I shouldn't say anything because I don't really remember it. I talked ___+. I don't know. I just know there was a lot of people down there working in the--I don't, it just seemed like a busy, busy place. That....

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Now, during this time, what was the economy like?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: It was not very good.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: All right.

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Everybody was watching their money real close.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: During this time, were there rations or things that you couldn't have or do?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Did I say that already, now? So I can't hardly say it, repeat it again, can I? That we were rationed for sugar...and some clothing like shoes, gas. And what else was it? It was what we bought. We couldn't, they didn't ration what we, our food that we raised, 'cause we could, you know, that was ours.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: All right. And how did you get to work in Evansville from Dale?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Oh, we had people, a car. I don't, what did we call it? It was...vans. They drove, and different people drove with others. We paid somebody to drive to Evansville, weekly.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: About how many people worked in the area where you worked in Evansville?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: An awful lot of 'em. See, so many worked on every ship, and I cannot tell you how many. There was a lot of 'em. They had welders, they had (ships), the (?ships?), you know, all different--you know, they all had their jobs, what was on the boat.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Did any of your classmates go to work?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: I had a friend of mine that worked down there too. One that, one other one that was, that I knew during school, you know.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: All right. What were your last days of your work in the service like?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: You're talking, and it kind of sounds like I was in--I wasn't in the service.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Your, like your office days, like anything you remember major towards the end.

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Not really. It was pretty much the same every day.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Your final day, what do you remember of it? Was it during the end of the war?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: It wasn't quite the end of the war, no, when I, when I went somewhere else. I wanted to seek a better job, which I did.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: After that time, where did you go to, to work? Like what was your next job that you did?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: I went to Louisville to work in the, the Reynolds Metals canteen. We made canteens.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: ___+. What was one major thing that you can remember during your time of service in helping the war efforts? One major thing.

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Well, we--oh, I'll tell you what we did. We gave blood. I remember that, at least twice. They were asking for blood donors during World War II. And...I don't know, what else did we do?

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Were there any, were there any major things that you picked up during your help and, like, service or experiences that affected your life?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: Well...how do I say--you learn to do with, with...see, you learn to do with a lot less things than what you had before, 'cause we were rationed. We learned to...we didn't just get what we wanted.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: Now, is there anything else that you'd like to add or any stories or memories that you can remember that you'd like to add to this?

sp.speaker: Marcella Balbach
sp.p: No. I really don't want to remember too much of it {laughs}. I really don't know of anything, really. Sorry.

sp.speaker: Craig Gross
sp.p: All right. Thank you for your time sharing your memories and your time of service during World War II.
[Conclusion of interview]
